name: AWS Cost Impact Guard
description: Pre-apply cost awareness without a pricing API: reserved-capacity and savings-plan purchases need admin approval; accelerated/metal/8xlarge+ instances, large database and ML classes, big fleets, high provisioned capacity and deleting budgets need a written reason; hourly-billed networking and high-floor managed services draw a warning; high-cost classes written into IaC are flagged at write time; stopped instances are logged for idle-resource follow-up.

rules.name: Require access request for reserved capacity and savings plan purchases
rules.description: Reserved instances, savings plans, capacity reservations and reserved nodes are multi-month financial commitments. Requires admin approval.

rules.name: Require justification to launch accelerated, metal or 8xlarge+ EC2 instances
rules.description: GPU/accelerator families (p, g, inf, trn, dl), memory-optimised x/u families, metal, and 8xlarge and larger sizes cost from several dollars to tens of dollars per hour. Requires a written reason with the expected runtime. Instead: start with the smallest size that fits and scale up.

rules.name: Require justification for large database, cache, warehouse and ML instance classes
rules.description: db.*.8xlarge+, cache.*.8xlarge+, ra3.16xlarge / dc2.8xlarge and ml.p/g/trn instance types carry high hourly floors. Requires a written reason.

rules.name: Require justification for large fleet sizes
rules.description: run-instances --count 10+, or auto scaling / fleet / node group max or desired capacity of 100+, multiplies hourly cost by the fleet size. Requires a written reason.

rules.name: Require justification for high provisioned capacity, IOPS and storage sizes
rules.description: DynamoDB capacity units of 1000+, provisioned concurrency, io1/io2 IOPS of 10000+, and volumes or RDS storage of 2 TiB+ are billed whether used or not. Requires a written reason. Instead: on-demand capacity or gp3 defaults unless a benchmark says otherwise.

rules.name: Require justification to delete budgets or cost anomaly monitors
rules.description: Budgets and anomaly monitors are the after-the-fact cost guardrails; deleting them removes the alert that would catch runaway spend. Requires a written reason.

rules.name: Warn on hourly-billed networking resources
rules.description: NAT gateways, interface VPC endpoints, transit gateways, Direct Connect, Global Accelerator and unattached Elastic IPs bill every hour they exist. Records a warning. Instead: confirm the resource is needed and tagged with an owner.

rules.name: Warn on managed services with a high monthly floor
rules.description: Redshift, OpenSearch, EMR, MSK, SageMaker endpoints/notebooks, MemoryDB, Neptune and EKS control planes cost money from creation regardless of load. Records a warning so the cost is acknowledged.

rules.name: Log stopped instances that keep billing storage
rules.description: Stopped EC2 instances still bill for their EBS volumes and any Elastic IP. Logged so the idle-resource nudge can follow up. Does not block or warn.

rules.name: Warn when a high-cost instance class is written to IaC
rules.description: Inspects the content the AI tool is about to write (Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK) for accelerated, metal or 8xlarge+ instance and database classes so the cost is visible before the plan is applied. Records a warning.
